modelEssay.title: Building Trust Between Teachers and Students
modelEssay.content:
Trust is the cornerstone of any successful educational relationship. In classrooms where trust is fostered, students are more likely to engage actively, take risks, and learn effectively. This bond is crucial for both teachers and students to thrive.

Firstly, trust encourages open communication. When students trust their teachers, they feel safe to ask questions, voice opinions, and admit when they do not understand something. This openness facilitates learning and promotes a positive classroom environment. Moreover, a trusting relationship can also boost students' self-esteem and motivation, as they feel valued and supported. Teachers, in turn, benefit from trust as it allows them to provide constructive feedback without fear of alienating their students.

In conclusion, building trust between teachers and students is essential for educational success. It fosters an environment where learning can flourish, and both parties can grow and develop. To cultivate this trust, it is important for teachers to be approachable, fair, and consistent, while students should be encouraged to be open and respectful.

transcript.text: Tonight we have a special guest from a local establishment, the Parisian Café.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今晚我们有一位来自当地一家机构“巴黎咖啡馆”的特别嘉宾。

transcript.text: Welcome.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 欢迎。

transcript.text: Hi, thanks for having me on your show.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗨，感谢邀请我来到你的节目。

transcript.text: Thank you for joining us.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 感谢你的加入。

transcript.text: So please tell us, why did you decide to open a café?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么请告诉我们，你为什么决定开一家咖啡馆？

transcript.text: Well, we saw the opportunity to offer something a little special and different from other establishments.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，我们看到了一个机会，可以提供一些与其它场所不同的特别之处。

transcript.text: Cafés certainly are a very competitive market sector.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 咖啡馆无疑是一个竞争非常激烈的市场领域。

transcript.text: There are more than plenty in our city and we felt they are all rather similar to each other.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们城市里咖啡馆非常多，我们觉得它们彼此都相当相似。

transcript.text: Wouldn't you agree?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你不同意吗？

transcript.text: Certainly, yes.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 当然，是的。

transcript.text: So how is your establishment any different?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那么你的场所有何不同？

transcript.text: Well, simply put, we have rabbits wandering freely around the place.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 嗯，简单来说，我们让兔子在场所里自由游荡。

transcript.text: Our customers come in and enjoy their food and drinks, while little rabbits play about and brush against their legs.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们的顾客进来享受食物和饮料，而小兔子在玩耍，蹭他们的腿。

transcript.text: There's no other place like it.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 没有其他地方像这样。

transcript.text: That's amazing.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这太棒了。

transcript.text: How did you come up with the idea?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你是怎么想到这个主意的？

transcript.text: We saw other cafés with cats in them, so we thought, why not rabbits?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们看到其他咖啡馆里有猫，所以我们想，为什么不是兔子呢？

transcript.text: People love rabbits.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 人们喜欢兔子。

transcript.text: They are very cute animals.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 它们是非常可爱的动物。

transcript.text: But is it safe?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但这安全吗？

transcript.text: Do the rabbits ever bite people or do any customers ever hurt the rabbits?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 兔子会咬人吗，或者有顾客会伤害兔子吗？

transcript.text: It's perfectly safe for both the rabbits and our customers.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这对兔子和我们的顾客都非常安全。

transcript.text: Rabbits are very peaceful and certainly do not bite.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 兔子非常温和，当然不会咬人。

transcript.text: Furthermore, our rabbits are regularly cleaned and have all received the required shots, so there is no health risk whatsoever.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 此外，我们的兔子定期清洁，并且都接受了必要的疫苗注射，所以没有任何健康风险。

transcript.text: As for our customers, they are all animal lovers, so they would never try to hurt the rabbits.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 至于我们的顾客，他们都是动物爱好者，所以永远不会试图伤害兔子。

transcript.text: Sometimes a young child may get over-excited and be a little too rough, but it's never a serious matter.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 有时小孩可能会过于兴奋，有点粗暴，但这从来不是严重的问题。

transcript.text: On the contrary, the Parisian café offers a great experience for children, a chance for them to learn about rabbits and how to take care of them.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 相反，巴黎咖啡馆为孩子们提供了一次很好的体验，让他们有机会了解兔子以及如何照顾它们。

transcript.text: Well, it's certainly the first time I've heard of a café like that.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 嗯，这肯定是我第一次听说这样的咖啡馆。

transcript.text: So unhealthy.

transcript.translation: 没错。

transcript.text: And these big food corporations have so much money to spend on clever tactics designed to make young children want to buy their products.

transcript.text: Children never stand a chance.

transcript.translation: 这真的很不公平。

transcript.text: You are so right.

transcript.translation: 段落一。

transcript.text: The Nile, which begins in central Africa and flows over 4,100 miles north into the Mediterranean, hosted one of the world's great ancient civilizations along its shores.
transcript.translation: 尼罗河发源于非洲中部，向北流淌超过4,100英里注入地中海，沿岸孕育了世界上最伟大的古代文明之一。

transcript.text: Calm and peaceful for most of the year, the Nile used to flood annually, thereby creating, irrigating and carrying new topsoil to the nearby farmland on which ancient Egypt depended for livelihood.
transcript.translation: 尼罗河一年中大部分时间平静安宁，过去每年都会泛滥，从而创造、灌溉并带来新的表层土壤到附近的农田，古埃及依赖这些农田为生。

transcript.text: As a means of transportation, the river carried various vessels up and down its length.
transcript.translation: 作为交通工具，这条河流承载着各种船只在其全长上下航行。

transcript.text: A journey through the unobstructed part of this waterway today would pass by the splendid Valley of the Kings, where the tombs of many of these ancient monarchs have stood for over 3,000 years.
transcript.translation: 如今，沿着这条水道畅通无阻的部分旅行，会经过壮丽的国王谷，那里许多古代君主的陵墓已经矗立了超过3,000年。

transcript.text: Great civilizations and intensive settlement are hardly associated with the Amazon.
transcript.translation: 伟大的文明和密集的定居点几乎与亚马逊河无关。

transcript.text: Yet this 4,000-mile-long South American river carries about 20% of the world's fresh water, more than the Mississippi, Nile and Yangtze combined.
transcript.translation: 然而，这条长4,000英里的南美洲河流承载着全球约20%的淡水，比密西西比河、尼罗河和长江的总和还要多。

transcript.text: Other statistics are equally astonishing.
transcript.translation: 其他统计数据同样令人惊讶。

transcript.text: The Amazon is so wide at some points that from its centre neither shore can be seen.
transcript.translation: 亚马逊河在某些地方非常宽阔，从其中心看不见任何岸。

transcript.text: Each second, the Amazon pours some 55 million gallons of water into the Atlantic.
transcript.translation: 每秒钟，亚马逊河向大西洋倾注约5,500万加仑的水。

transcript.text: There, at its mouth, stands one island larger than Switzerland.
transcript.translation: 在那里，在河口处，有一个比瑞士还大的岛屿。

transcript.text: Most important of all, the Amazon irrigates the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.
transcript.translation: 最重要的是，亚马逊河灌溉着地球上最大的热带雨林。

transcript.text: How often do you say to people, I'm busy or I haven't got time for that?

transcript.text: It's an inevitable truth that all of us live a life in the fast lane, even though we know that being busy is not always particularly healthy.
transcript.translation: 一个不可避免的事实是，我们所有人都生活在快节奏中，即使我们知道忙碌并不总是特别健康。

transcript.text: Growing up in New Zealand, everything was always calm and slow.

transcript.text: People enjoyed the tranquility of a slower pace of life.

transcript.text: But after I moved to Tokyo and lived there for a number of years, I got used to having a pile of to-do lists, and my calendar always looked like a mess with loads of things to do written across it.
transcript.translation: 但在我搬到东京并在那里生活了几年后，我习惯了有一堆待办事项清单，我的日历总是看起来乱七八糟，上面写满了要做的事情。

transcript.text: I found myself filling my time up with endless work meetings and social events, rushing along as busy as a bee.
transcript.translation: 我发现自己用无尽的工作会议和社交活动填满时间，忙碌得像蜜蜂一样匆忙。

transcript.text: Then, one day, I came across a book called In Praise of Slowness, and realised that being busy is not only detrimental, but also has the danger of turning life into an endless race.
transcript.translation: 然后，有一天，我偶然发现了一本名为《慢的赞美》的书，并意识到忙碌不仅有害，还可能将生活变成一场无休止的竞赛。

transcript.text: So I started practising the various practical steps mentioned by the author in the book, and began to revolt against the very idea of being too busy.
transcript.translation: 因此，我开始实践作者在书中提到的各种实用步骤，并开始反抗过度忙碌的观念。

transcript.text: It doesn't mean that my to-do lists no longer exist, but I've become more aware of the importance of slowing down, and making sure that I enjoy the daily activities as I carry them out.
transcript.translation: 这并不意味着我的待办事项清单不再存在，但我变得更加意识到放慢速度的重要性，并确保在执行日常活动时享受它们。

transcript.text: From now on, when someone asks you how your life is, try responding with words like exciting and fun, instead of the cultural norm that says busy.
transcript.translation: 从现在起，当有人问你生活如何时，试着用‘令人兴奋的’和‘有趣的’这样的词来回应，而不是文化规范中常说的‘忙碌’。

transcript.text: Governments, private groups and individuals spend billions of dollars a year trying to root out non-native organisms that are considered dangerous to ecosystems, and to prevent the introduction of new intruders.
transcript.translation: 政府、私人团体和个人每年花费数十亿美元，试图根除被认为对生态系统危险的非本地生物，并防止新入侵者的引入。

transcript.text: But a number of scientists question the assumption that the presence of alien species can never be acceptable in a natural ecosystem.
transcript.translation: 但许多科学家质疑这一假设，即外来物种的存在在自然生态系统中永远是不可接受的。

transcript.text: They say that portraying introduced species as inherently bad is an unscientific approach.
transcript.translation: 他们说，将引入物种描绘为本质上不好是不科学的做法。

transcript.text: Distinctions between exotic and native species are artificial, said Dr.
transcript.translation: 外来物种和本地物种之间的区别是人为的，博士说。

transcript.text: Michael Rosenzweig, a professor of evolutionary biology at the University of Arizona.
transcript.translation: 迈克尔·罗森茨维格，亚利桑那大学进化生物学教授。

transcript.text: Because they depend on picking a date and calling the plants and animals that show up after that date exotic.
transcript.translation: 因为它们依赖于选择一个日期，并将在该日期之后出现的植物和动物称为外来物种。

transcript.text: Ecosystems free of species defined as exotic are, by default, considered the most natural.
transcript.translation: 没有被定义为外来物种的生态系统，默认被认为是最自然的。

transcript.text: You can't roll back the clock and remove all exotics or fix habitats, Dr.
transcript.translation: 你不能倒转时钟并移除所有外来物种或修复栖息地，博士说。

transcript.text: Rosenzweig said.
transcript.translation: 罗森茨维格说。

transcript.text: Both native and exotic species can become invasive, and so they all have to be monitored and controlled when they begin to get out of hand.
transcript.translation: 本地物种和外来物种都可能变得具有入侵性，因此当它们开始失控时，都必须进行监控和控制。

transcript.text: At its core, the debate is about how to manage the world's remaining natural ecosystems and about how and how much to restore other habitats.
transcript.translation: 核心在于，这场辩论是关于如何管理世界上剩余的自然生态系统，以及如何恢复其他栖息地和恢复多少。

transcript.text: Species that invade a territory can harm ecosystems, agriculture and human health.
transcript.translation: 入侵一个地区的物种可能危害生态系统、农业和人类健康。

transcript.text: They can threaten some native species or even destroy and replace others.
transcript.translation: 它们可能威胁一些本地物种，甚至摧毁和替代其他物种。

transcript.text: Next to habitat loss, these invasive species represent the greatest threat to biodiversity worldwide, many ecologists say.
transcript.translation: 许多生态学家说，除了栖息地丧失，这些入侵物种代表着全球生物多样性面临的最大威胁。

transcript.text: Ecologists generally define an alien species as one that people accidentally or deliberately carried to its new location.
transcript.translation: 生态学家通常将外来物种定义为人们意外或故意带到新地点的物种。

transcript.text: Across the American continents, exotic species are those introduced after the first European contact.
transcript.translation: 在美洲大陆，外来物种是指在欧洲首次接触后引入的物种。

transcript.text: That date, rounded off to 1500 AD, represents what ecologists consider to have been a major shift in the spread of species, including crops and livestock, as they began to migrate with humans from continent to continent.
transcript.translation: 这个日期大约定在公元1500年，代表了生态学家认为物种传播的重大转变，包括农作物和牲畜，随着它们开始随人类从一个大陆迁移到另一个大陆。

transcript.text: Only a small percentage of alien species cause problems in their new habitats, said Don Smith, professor of ecology and evolutionary biology at the University of Tennessee.
transcript.translation: 田纳西大学生态学和进化生物学教授唐·史密斯说，只有一小部分外来物种在其新栖息地造成问题。

transcript.text: Of the 7,000 alien species in the United States, out of a total of 150 ,000 species, only about 10% are invasive, he pointed out.
transcript.translation: 他指出，在美国150,000个物种中的7,000个外来物种中，只有约10%具有入侵性。

transcript.text: The other 90% have fit into their environments and are considered naturalized.
transcript.translation: 其他90%已经适应了环境，并被认为已经归化。

transcript.text: Yet appearances can deceive, ecologists caution, and many of these exotics may be considered acceptable only because no one has documented their harmful effects.
transcript.translation: 然而，生态学家警告说，外表可能具有欺骗性，许多外来物种之所以被认为可接受，可能仅仅是因为没有人记录其有害影响。

transcript.text: What is more, non-native species can appear harmless for decades, then turn invasive.
transcript.translation: 更重要的是，非本地物种可能几十年看起来无害，然后变成入侵物种。

transcript.text: Good morning ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the third in our series of business seminars in the programme Doing Business Abroad.
transcript.translation: 女士们、先生们，早上好，欢迎参加我们“海外业务”系列商业研讨会的第三讲。

transcript.text: Today we are going to look at intercultural awareness, that is, the fact that not everyone is British, not everyone speaks English, and not everyone does business in a British way.
transcript.translation: 今天我们将探讨跨文化意识，即不是每个人都是英国人，不是每个人都会说英语，也不是每个人都以英国方式做生意。

transcript.text: And why should they?
transcript.translation: 他们为什么要这样做呢？

transcript.text: If overseas business people are selling to us, then they will make every effort to speak English and to respect our traditions and methods.
transcript.translation: 如果海外商人向我们销售产品，他们会尽力说英语，并尊重我们的传统和方法。

transcript.text: It is only polite for us to do the same when we visit them.
transcript.translation: 当我们访问他们时，同样做也是礼貌的。

transcript.text: It is not only polite, it is essential if we want to sell British products overseas.
transcript.translation: 这不仅是礼貌的，如果我们想在海外销售英国产品，这也是必要的。

transcript.text: First, a short quiz.
transcript.translation: 首先，一个小测试。

transcript.text: Let's see how interculturally aware you are.
transcript.translation: 让我们看看你的跨文化意识有多强。

transcript.translation: 在每月的1号和7号，你在哪里不能饮酒？

transcript.text: OK, everyone had a chance to make some notes?
transcript.translation: 好的，大家都已经做笔记了吗？

transcript.text: Right, here are the answers.
transcript.translation: 好的，这里是答案。

transcript.text: Although I am sure that the information could equally well apply to countries other than those I have chosen.
transcript.translation: 虽然我确信这些信息同样适用于我所选国家之外的其他国家。

transcript.text: So, number 1.

transcript.text: You must not drink alcohol on the 1st and 7th of the month in India.
transcript.translation: 在印度，你不能在每月的1号和7号饮酒。

transcript.text: In international hotels you may find it served, but if you are having a meal with an Indian colleague, remember to avoid asking for a beer if your arrival coincides with one of those dates.
transcript.translation: 在国际酒店，你可能会发现有酒供应，但如果你和一位印度同事一起用餐，记住如果你的到达日期恰逢这些日期之一，要避免要啤酒。

transcript.text: In Arab countries, the politeness and generosity of the people is without parallel.
transcript.translation: 在阿拉伯国家，人们的礼貌和慷慨是无与伦比的。

transcript.text: If you admire your colleague's beautiful golden bowls, you may well find yourself being presented with them as a present.

transcript.text: This is not a cheap way to do your shopping, however, as your host will quite correctly expect you to respond by presenting him with a gift of equal worth and beauty.

transcript.text: Shortly after he took over the Reader's Digest Association in 1984, George Gruen unlocked the company's boardroom and announced that the room was now open to the employees.
transcript.translation: 1984年，乔治·格伦接管读者文摘协会后不久，他打开了公司的董事会会议室，并宣布该会议室现在向员工开放。

transcript.text: It was a symbolic act, indicating that under Gruen's leadership, Reader's Digest was going to be different.
transcript.translation: 这是一个象征性的举动，表明在格伦的领导下，读者文摘将有所不同。

transcript.text: True to his word, Gruen has shaken up the culture here.
transcript.translation: 格伦信守诺言，震撼了这里的文化。

transcript.text: To get an idea of the culture we're talking about, consider the boardroom Gruen opened up.
transcript.translation: 要了解我们所谈论的文化，请考虑格伦开放的那个董事会会议室。

transcript.text: It has artworks that any museum in the world would want to collect, paintings by many world-famous artists like Monet and Picasso.
transcript.translation: 那里有世界上任何博物馆都想收藏的艺术品，包括许多世界著名艺术家如莫奈和毕加索的画作。

transcript.text: Its headquarters houses some 3,000 works of art.
transcript.translation: 其总部收藏了约3000件艺术品。

transcript.text: The main building is topped with a Georgian tower with four sculptures of the mythical winged horse, the magazine's corporate logo.
transcript.translation: 主楼上有一座乔治亚风格的塔，塔上有四尊神话中的有翼马的雕像，这是该杂志的企业标识。

transcript.text: It sits on 127 acres of well-trimmed lawns.
transcript.translation: 它坐落在127英亩修剪整齐的草坪上。

transcript.text: The editor's office used to be occupied by founder DeWitt Wallace, who, along with his wife, Leila Aitchison Wallace, launched Reader's Digest in 1922 with condensed articles from other publications.
transcript.translation: 编辑办公室曾由创始人德威特·华莱士使用，他与妻子莱拉·艾奇逊·华莱士于1922年创办了《读者文摘》，内容来自其他出版物的缩写文章。

transcript.text: It has become the world's most widely read magazine, selling 28 million copies each month in 17 languages and 41 different editions.
transcript.translation: 它已成为世界上阅读量最广泛的杂志，每月以17种语言和41个不同版本销售2800万份。

transcript.text: The Wallaces, both children of church ministers, had a clearly defined formula for their little magazine, as Reader's Digest was originally subtitled.
transcript.translation: 华莱士夫妇都是牧师的孩子，他们为这本小杂志（《读者文摘》最初有副标题）制定了明确的编辑原则。

transcript.text: Articles were to be short, readable, and uplifting.
transcript.translation: 文章要简短、易读且鼓舞人心。

transcript.text: Subjects were picked to inspire or entertain.
transcript.translation: 主题要能启发或娱乐。

transcript.text: The Wallaces didn't accept advertising in the U .
transcript.translation: 华莱士夫妇在美

transcript.text: S.
transcript.translation: 国

transcript.text: edition until 1955, and even then they didn't allow any ads for cigarettes, liquor, or drugs.
transcript.translation: 版直到1955年，即使那时他们也不允许任何香烟、酒类或药物的广告。

transcript.text: The Wallaces also had a clear sense of the kind of workplace they wanted.
transcript.translation: 华莱士夫妇也清楚他们想要什么样的工作场所。

transcript.text: It started as a mom-and-pop operation, and the childless Wallaces always considered employees to be part of their family.
transcript.translation: 它最初是一家夫妻店式的企业，没有孩子的华莱士夫妇总是将员工视为家人的一部分。

transcript.text: Employees still tell stories of how the Wallaces would take care of employees who had met with misfortunes, and they showered their employees with unusual benefits, like a turkey at Thanksgiving and Fridays off in May.
transcript.translation: 员工们仍然讲述华莱士夫妇如何照顾遭遇不幸的员工的故事，他们给员工提供不寻常的福利，比如感恩节的火鸡和五月的星期五休假。

transcript.text: This cozy workplace no longer exists here.
transcript.translation: 这种温馨的工作场所在这里已不复存在。

transcript.text: The Wallaces both died in their 90s in the early 1980s.
transcript.translation: 华莱士夫妇都在1980年代初90多岁时去世。

transcript.text: George Gruen, a former ad salesman who joined Reader's Digest in 1960, has his eye focused on the bottom line.
transcript.translation: 乔治·格伦曾是广告销售员，于1960年加入《读者文摘》，他专注于底线利润。

transcript.text: In a few short years, he turned the magazine on its head.
transcript.translation: 在短短几年内，他彻底改变了这本杂志。

transcript.text: He laid off several hundred workers.
transcript.translation: 他裁减了数百名工人。

transcript.text: Especially hard-hit were the blue and pink-collar departments, such as subscription fulfillment.

paragraphs.text: Did Sarah Josepha Hale write "Mary 's Little Lamb," the eternal nursery rhyme (儿歌) about a girl named Mary with a stubborn lamb? This is still dispute, but it's clear that the woman __26__ for writing it was one of America 's most fascinating __27__. In honor of the poem 's publication on May 24,1830, here's more about the __28__ author 's life.
paragraphs.translation: 萨拉·约瑟法·黑尔写了《玛丽的小羊羔》这首永恒的儿歌吗？这首儿歌是关于一个名叫玛丽的女孩和一只固执的小羊的故事。这仍然存在争议，但很明显，被认为写了这首诗的女人是美国最迷人的角色之一。为纪念这首诗于1830年5月24日发表，以下是更多关于这位假定作者生平的信息。

paragraphs.text: Hale wasn't just a writer, she was also a __29__ social advocate, and she was particularly __30__ with an ideal New England, which she associated with abundant Thanksgiving meals that she claimed had "a deep moral influence." She began a nationwide __31__ to have a national holiday declared that would bring families together while celebrating the __32__ festivals. In 1863, after 17 years of advocacy including letters to five presidents, Hale got it. President Abraham Lincoln, during the Civil War, issued a __33__ setting aside the last Thursday in November for the holiday.
paragraphs.translation: 黑尔不仅是一位作家，还是一位热切的社会倡导者，她特别迷恋一个理想的新英格兰，并将其与丰盛的感恩节餐食联系起来，她声称这些餐食具有“深刻的道德影响”。她发起了一场全国性的运动，要求宣布一个全国性节日，以在庆祝传统节日的同时让家人团聚。1863年，经过17年的倡导，包括写信给五位总统，黑尔成功了。亚伯拉罕·林肯总统在内战期间发布公告，将11月的最后一个星期四定为这个节日。

paragraphs.text: The true authorship of "Mary's Little Lamb" is disputed.. According to New England Historical Society, Hale wrote only one part of the poem, but claimed authorship. Regardless of the author, it seems that the poem was __34__ by a real event. When young Mary Sawyer was followed to school by a lamb in 1816, it caused some problems. A bystander named John Roulstone wrote a poem about the event, then, at some point, Hale herself seems to have helped write it. However, if a 1916 piece by her great-niece is to be trusted, Hale claimed for the __35__ of her life that "Some other people pretended that someone else wrote the poem".
paragraphs.translation: 《玛丽的小羊羔》的真正作者身份存在争议。根据新英格兰历史学会的说法，黑尔只写了这首诗的一部分，但声称拥有著作权。无论作者是谁，这首诗似乎是受真实事件启发的。1816年，当年轻的玛丽·索耶被一只小羊跟着去上学时，这引起了一些问题。一位名叫约翰·鲁尔斯通的旁观者写了关于这个事件的诗，然后，在某个时候，黑尔本人似乎帮助写了它。然而，如果她侄孙女在1916年的一篇文章可信的话，黑尔一生中都声称“其他人假装这首诗是别人写的”。

questionGroups.title: Grow Plants Without Water

paragraphs.text: Ever since humanity began to farm our own food, we've faced the unpredictable rain that is both friend and enemy. It comes and goes without much warning, and a field of lush (茂盛的) leafy greens one year can dry up and blow away the next. Food security and fortunes depend on sufficient rain, and nowhere more so than in Africa, where 96% of farmland depends on rain instead of the irrigation common in more developed places. It has consequences : South Africa's ongoing drought— the worst in three decades— will cost at least a quarter of its corn crop this year.
paragraphs.translation: 自人类开始种植粮食以来，我们一直面临着既友好又敌对的不可预测的雨水。它来去无常，一片茂盛的绿叶蔬菜田可能在下一年就干枯并被风吹走。粮食安全和财富依赖于充足的雨水，这一点在非洲尤为突出，那里96%的农田依赖雨水而非更发达地区常见的灌溉。其后果是：南非持续的干旱——三十年来最严重的一次——将使其今年玉米作物损失至少四分之一。

paragraphs.text: Biologist Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town in South Africa says that nature has plenty of answers for people who want to grow crops in places with unpredictable rainfall. She is hard at work finding a way to take traits from rare wild plants that adapt to extreme dry weather and use them in food crops. As the earth's climate changes and rainfall becomes even less predictable in some places, those answers will grow even more valuable. "The type of farming I'm aiming for is literally so that people can survive as it's going to get more and more dry," Farrant says.
paragraphs.translation: 南非开普敦大学的生物学家吉尔·法伦特表示，对于那些想在降雨不可预测的地方种植作物的人来说，大自然有许多答案。她正在努力寻找一种方法，从适应极端干旱天气的稀有野生植物中提取特性，并将其应用于粮食作物。随着地球气候变化和某些地区降雨变得更加不可预测，这些答案将变得更有价值。法伦特说：“我所追求的农业类型，字面意义上是为了让人们在日益干旱的环境中生存下来。”

paragraphs.text: Extreme conditions produce extremely tough plants. In the rusty red deserts of South Africa, steep-sided rocky hills called inselbergs rear up from the plains like the bones of the earth. The hills are remnants of an earlier geological era, scraped bare of most soil and exposed to the elements. Yet on these and similar formations in deserts around the world, a few fierce plants have adapted to endure under ever-changing conditions.
paragraphs.translation: 极端条件产生极其坚韧的植物。在南非锈红色的沙漠中，陡峭的岩石山丘称为岛山，像大地的骨架一样从平原上突起。这些山丘是更早地质时代的遗迹，被剥离了大部分土壤，暴露在自然环境中。然而，在这些以及世界各地沙漠中的类似地貌上，一些顽强的植物已经适应了在不断变化的条件下生存。

paragraphs.text: Farrant calls them resurrection plants (复苏植物). During months without water under a harsh sun. They wither, shrink and contract until they look like a pile of dead gray leaves. But rainfall can revive them in a matter of hours. Her time-lapse (间歇性拍摄的) videos of the revivals look like someone playing a tape of the plant's death in reverse.
paragraphs.translation: 法伦特称它们为复苏植物。在严酷阳光下数月无水期间，它们枯萎、收缩，直到看起来像一堆死灰色的叶子。但降雨可以在几小时内使它们复苏。她拍摄的复苏过程的时间推移视频看起来像有人倒放了植物死亡的录像带。

paragraphs.text: The big difference between "drought-tolerant" plants and these tough plants: metabolism. Many different kinds of plants have developed tactics to weather dry spells. Some plants store reserves of water to see them through a drought ; others send roots deep down to subsurface water supplies. But once these plants use up their stored reserve or tap out the underground supply, they cease growing and start to die. They may be able to handle a drought of some length, and many people use the term "drought tolerant" to describe such plants, but they never actually stop needing to consume water, so Farrant prefers to call them drought resistant.
paragraphs.translation: “耐旱”植物与这些坚韧植物之间的主要区别在于新陈代谢。许多不同种类的植物已经发展出应对干旱期的策略。一些植物储存水分储备以度过干旱；另一些植物将根深扎以获取地下水供应。但一旦这些植物用尽储存的储备或耗尽地下供应，它们就会停止生长并开始死亡。它们可能能够应对一定长度的干旱，许多人用“耐旱”来形容这类植物，但它们实际上从未停止需要消耗水分，所以法伦特更倾向于称它们为抗旱植物。

paragraphs.text: Resurrection plants, defined as those capable of recovering from holding less than 0.1 grams of water per gram of dry mass, are different. They lack water-storing structures, and their existence on rock faces prevents them from tapping groundwater, so they have instead developed the ability to change their metabolism. When they detect an extended dry period, they divert their metabolisms, producing sugars and certain stress-associated proteins and other materials in their tissues. As the plant dries, these resources take on first the properties of honey, then rubber, and finally enter a glass-like state that is "the most stable state that the plant can maintain," Farrant says. That slows the plant's metabolism and protects its dried-out tissues. The plants also change shape, shrinking to minimize the surface area through which their remaining water might evaporate. They can recover from months and years without water, depending on the species.
paragraphs.translation: 复苏植物，定义为那些能够从每克干物质持有少于0.1克水分的状态中恢复的植物，是不同的。它们缺乏储水结构，并且它们在岩石表面的存在阻止了它们获取地下水，因此它们反而发展出了改变新陈代谢的能力。当它们探测到延长的干旱期时，它们会改变新陈代谢，在组织中产生糖类、某些应激相关蛋白质和其他物质。随着植物干燥，这些资源首先具有蜂蜜的特性，然后是橡胶，最后进入玻璃状状态，这是“植物能够维持的最稳定状态”，法伦特说。这减缓了植物的新陈代谢并保护其干燥组织。植物还会改变形状，收缩以最小化剩余水分可能蒸发的表面积。根据物种不同，它们可以从数月甚至数年的无水状态中恢复。

paragraphs.text: What else can do this dry-out-and-revive trick? Seeds-almost all of them. At the start of her career, Farrant studied. recalcitrant seeds (执拗性种子)," such as avocados, coffee and lychee. While tasty, such seeds are delicate--they cannot bud and grow if they dry out (as you may know if you've ever tried to grow a tree from an avocado pit). In the seed world, that makes them rare, because most seeds from flowering plants are quite robust. Most seeds can wait out the dry, unwelcoming seasons until conditions are right and they sprout (发芽). Yet once they start growing, such plants seem not to retain the ability to hit the pause button on metabolism in their stems or leaves.
paragraphs.translation: 还有什么能玩转这种干枯与复苏的把戏？种子——几乎所有种子。在职业生涯初期，法伦特研究了执拗性种子，如鳄梨、咖啡和荔枝。虽然美味，但这类种子很脆弱——如果它们干燥了，就不能发芽生长（如果你曾尝试用鳄梨核种树，你可能知道这一点）。在种子世界中，这使得它们很罕见，因为开花植物的大部分种子相当坚韧。大多数种子可以等待干燥、不友好的季节过去，直到条件合适时发芽。然而，一旦它们开始生长，这些植物似乎不再保留其茎或叶中按下新陈代谢暂停按钮的能力。

paragraphs.text: After completing her Ph. D. on seeds, Farrant began investigating whether it might be possible to isolate the properties that make most seeds so resilient (迅速恢复活力的) and transfer them to other plant tissues. What Farrant and others have found over the past two decades is that there are many genes involved in resurrection plants' response to dryness. Many of them are the same that regulate how seeds become dryness-tolerant while still attached to their parent plants. Now they are trying to figure out what molecular signaling processes activate those seed-building genes in resurrection plants— and how to reproduce them in crops. "Most genes are regulated by a master set of genes,"Farrant says. "We're looking at gene promoters and what would be their master switch."
paragraphs.translation: 完成关于种子的博士学位后，法伦特开始研究是否有可能分离出使大多数种子如此坚韧的特性，并将它们转移到其他植物组织中。法伦特和其他人在过去二十年中发现，有许多基因参与了复苏植物对干旱的反应。其中许多基因与调控种子在仍附着于母体植物时如何变得耐旱的基因相同。现在，他们正在试图弄清楚哪些分子信号过程激活了复苏植物中的这些种子构建基因——以及如何在作物中重现它们。法伦特说：“大多数基因由一组主基因调控。我们正在研究基因启动子及其主开关。”

paragraphs.text: Once Farrant and her colleagues feel they have a better sense of which switches to throw, they will have to find the best way to do so in useful crops. "I'm trying three methods of breeding," Farrant says: conventional, genetic modification and gene editing. She says she is aware that plenty of people do not want to eat genetically modified crops, but she is pushing ahead with every available tool until one works. Farmers and consumers alike can choose whether or not to use whichever version prevails: "I'm giving people an option."
paragraphs.translation: 一旦法伦特和她的同事们觉得他们更清楚该启动哪些开关，他们将不得不找到在有用作物中实现这一目标的最佳方法。法伦特说：“我正在尝试三种育种方法：常规育种、基因改造和基因编辑。她说她意识到许多人不想吃转基因作物，但她正在使用每种可用工具推进，直到其中一种起作用。农民和消费者都可以选择是否使用哪个版本占优势：“我在给人们一个选择。”

paragraphs.text: Farrant and others in the resurrection business got together last year to discuss the best species of resurrection plant to use as a lab model. Just like medical researchers use rats to test ideas for human medical treatments, botanists use plants that are relatively easy to grow in a lab or greenhouse setting to test their ideas for related species. The Queensland rock violet is one of the best studied resurrection plants so far, with a draft genome (基因图谱) published last year by a Chinese team. Also last year, Farrant and colleagues published a detailed molecular study of another candidate, Xerophyta viscosa, a tough-as-nail south African plant with lily-like flowers, and she says that a genome is on the way. one or both of these models will help researchers test their ideas — so far mostly done in the lab— on test plots.
paragraphs.translation: 法伦特和其他从事复苏植物研究的人去年聚在一起，讨论用作实验室模型的最佳复苏植物物种。就像医学研究人员用老鼠测试人类医疗想法一样，植物学家使用相对容易在实验室或温室环境中生长的植物来测试他们对相关物种的想法。昆士兰岩紫罗兰是迄今为止研究最深入的复苏植物之一，去年一个中国团队发表了其草图基因组。同样在去年，法伦特和同事发表了对另一个候选物种Xerophyta viscosa的详细分子研究，这是一种坚韧的南非植物，花朵似百合，她说基因组即将完成。这些模型中的一种或两种将帮助研究人员在测试地块上测试他们的想法——到目前为止主要在实验室进行。

paragraphs.text: Understanding the basic science first is key. There are good reasons why crop plants do not use dryness defenses already. For instance, there's a high energy cost in switching from a regular metabolism to an almost-no-water metabolism. It will also be necessary to understand what sort of yield farmers might expect and to establish the plant's safety. "The yield is never going to be high, "Farrant says, so these plants will be targeted not at Iowa farmers trying to squeeze more cash out of high-yield fields, but subsistence farmers who need help to survive a drought like the present one in South Africa." My vision is for the subsistence farmer," Farrant says. "I'm targeting crops that are of African value."
paragraphs.translation: 首先理解基础科学是关键。作物植物不使用干旱防御有充分的理由。例如，从常规新陈代谢切换到几乎无水的新陈代谢具有高能量成本。还需要了解农民可能期望的产量，并确定植物的安全性。法伦特说：“产量永远不会高，”因此这些植物将针对的不是试图从高产田地榨取更多现金的爱荷华州农民，而是需要帮助以度过如南非当前干旱的自给自足农民。法伦特说：“我的愿景是针对自给自足的农民。”“我针对的是具有非洲价值的作物。”

questions.analysis: 该陈述对应段落C。段落C中提到'Yet on these and similar formations in deserts around the world, a few fierce plants have adapted to endure under ever-changing conditions'（然而在这些以及世界各地沙漠中类似的地形上，一些强悍的植物已经适应了在不断变化的条件下生存），这与陈述中的'There are a couple of plants tough and adaptable enough to survive on bare rocky hills and in deserts'（有一些植物足够坚韧和适应性强，能够在裸露的岩石山丘和沙漠中生存）相对应。关键词匹配：plants tough and adaptable对应fierce plants adapted，survive on bare rocky hills and in deserts对应endure under ever-changing conditions。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Human memory is notoriously unreliable. Even people with the sharpest facial-recognition skills can only remember so much.
paragraphs.translation: 人类记忆的不可靠性众所周知。即使拥有最敏锐面部识别能力的人，记忆容量也有限。

paragraphs.text: It's tough to quantify how good a person is at remembering. No one really knows how many different faces someone can recall, for example, but various estimates tend to hover in the thousands-based on the number of acquaintances a person might have.
paragraphs.translation: 量化一个人的记忆力好坏很困难。例如，没有人真正知道一个人能回忆起多少张不同的面孔，但各种估计往往在数千张左右——基于一个人可能拥有的熟人数量。

paragraphs.text: Machines aren't limited this way. Give the right computer a massive database of faces, and it can process what it sees-then recognize a face it's told to find-with remarkable speed and precision. This skill is what supports the enormous promise of facial-recognition software in the 21st century. It's also what makes contemporary surveillance systems so scary.
paragraphs.translation: 机器不受这种方式的限制。给合适的计算机一个庞大的面孔数据库，它就能以惊人的速度和精度处理所见内容——然后识别出被告知要找的面孔。这项技能支撑着面部识别软件在21世纪的巨大前景，也正是它使得当代监控系统如此可怕。

paragraphs.text: The thing is, machines still have limitations when it comes to facial recognition. And scientists are only just beginning to understand what those constraints are. To begin to figure out how computers are struggling, researchers at the University of Washington created a massive database of faces- they call it MegaFace- and tested a variety of facial-recognition algorithms (算法) as they scaled up in complexity. The idea was to test the machines on a database that included up to 1 million different images of nearly 700,000 different people-and not just a large database featuring a relatively small number of different faces, more consistent with what's been used in other research.
paragraphs.translation: 问题在于，机器在面部识别方面仍然存在局限性。科学家们才刚刚开始理解这些限制是什么。为了初步了解计算机的困难，华盛顿大学的研究人员创建了一个庞大的面部数据库——他们称之为MegaFace——并测试了各种随着复杂性增加的面部识别算法。这个想法是在一个包含近70万人的高达100万张不同图像的数据库上测试机器，而不仅仅是一个拥有相对较少不同面孔的大型数据库，这与其他研究中使用的更一致。

paragraphs.text: As the databases grew, machine accuracy dipped across the board. Algorithms that were right 95% of the time when they were dealing with a 13, 000-image database, for example, were accurate about 70% of the time when confronted with 1 million images. That's still pretty good, says one of the researchers, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman."Much better than we expected, "she said.
paragraphs.translation: 随着数据库的增长，机器准确率全面下降。例如，在处理13,000张图像数据库时正确率为95%的算法，在面对100万张图像时准确率约为70%。一位研究人员Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman说，这仍然相当不错。"比我们预期的要好得多，"她说。

paragraphs.text: Machines also had difficulty adjusting for people who look a lot alike-either doppelgangers(长相极相似的人), whom the machine would have trouble identifying as two separate people, or the same person who appeared in different photos at different ages or in different lighting, whom the machine would incorrectly view as separate people.
paragraphs.translation: 机器也难以调整那些长相非常相似的人——无论是双胞胎（长相极相似的人），机器会难以将他们识别为两个不同的人，还是同一个人出现在不同年龄或不同光线下的照片中，机器会错误地将他们视为不同的人。

paragraphs.text: "Once we scale up, algorithms must be sensitive to tiny changes in identities and at the same time invariant to lighting, pose, age, "Kemelmacher-Shlizerman said.
paragraphs.translation: Kemelmacher-Shlizerman说："一旦我们扩大规模，算法必须对身份的细微变化敏感，同时对光线、姿势、年龄保持不变性。"

paragraphs.text: The trouble is, for many of the researchers who'd like to design systems to address these challenges, massive datasets for experimentation just don't exist--at least, not in formats that are accessible to academic researchers. Training sets like the ones Google and Facebook have are private. There are no public databases that contain millions of faces. MegaFace's creators say it's the largest publicly available facial-recognition dataset out there.
paragraphs.translation: 麻烦的是，对于许多希望设计系统来应对这些挑战的研究人员来说，用于实验的大规模数据集根本不存在——至少，不是以学术研究人员可访问的格式存在。像Google和Facebook拥有的训练集是私有的。没有包含数百万张面孔的公开数据库。MegaFace的创建者说它是目前最大的公开可用面部识别数据集。

paragraphs.text: "An ultimate face recognition algorithm should perform with billions of people in a dataset, "the researchers wrote.
paragraphs.translation: 研究人员写道："一个终极的面部识别算法应该能在包含数十亿人的数据集中表现良好。"

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: There're currently 21.5 million students in America, and many will be funding their college on borrowed money. Given that there's now over $1.3 trillion in student loans on the books, it's pretty clear that many students are far from sensible. The average student's debt upon graduation now approaches $40, 000, and as college becomes ever more expensive, calls to make it "free" are multiplying. Even Hillary Clinton says that when it comes to college, "Costs won't be a barrier. "
paragraphs.translation: 目前美国有2150万学生，许多人将通过借款来资助大学教育。鉴于目前学生贷款总额超过1.3万亿美元，很明显许多学生远非明智。学生毕业时的平均债务接近4万美元，随着大学费用越来越高，呼吁使其“免费”的声音不断增多。甚至希拉里·克林顿也说，当涉及到大学时，“费用不会成为障碍。”

paragraphs.text: But the only way college could be free is if the faculty and staff donated their time, the buildings required no maintenance, and campuses required no utilities. As long as it's impossible to produce something from nothing, costs are absolutely a barrier.
paragraphs.translation: 但大学免费的唯一方式是教职员工捐赠时间、建筑无需维护、校园无需设施。只要无法无中生有，费用绝对是一个障碍。

paragraphs.text: The actual question we debate is who should pay for people to go to college. If taxpayers are to bear the cost of forgiving student loans, shouldn't they have a say in how their money is used?
paragraphs.translation: 我们实际辩论的问题是谁应该为人们上大学买单。如果纳税人要承担免除学生贷款的费用，他们难道不应该对如何使用他们的钱有发言权吗？

paragraphs.text: At least taxpayers should be able to decide what students will study on the public dime. If we're going to force taxpayers to foot the bill for college degrees, students should only study those subjects that're of greatest benefit to taxpayers. After all, students making their own choices in this respect is what caused the problem in the first place. We simply don't need more poetry, gender studies, or sociology majors. How do we know which subjects benefit society? Easy.
paragraphs.translation: 至少纳税人应该能够决定学生用公共资金学什么。如果我们要强迫纳税人支付大学学位的费用，学生应该只学习那些对纳税人最有益的科目。毕竟，学生在这方面的自主选择正是导致问题的根本原因。我们根本不需要更多的诗歌、性别研究或社会学专业。我们如何知道哪些科目对社会有益？很简单。

paragraphs.text: Average starting salaries give a clear indication of what type of training society needs its new workers to have. Certainly, there're benefits to a college major beyond the job a student can perform. But if we're talking about the benefits to society, the only thing that matters is what the major enables the student to produce for society. And the value of what the student can produce is reflected in the wage employers are willing to pay the student to produce it.
paragraphs.translation: 平均起薪清楚地表明社会需要新员工接受何种培训。当然，大学专业的好处不仅仅限于学生能从事的工作。但如果我们谈论对社会的好处，唯一重要的是专业使学生能为社会生产什么。而学生能生产的东西的价值体现在雇主愿意支付给学生的工资上。

paragraphs.text: A low wage for elementary school teachers, however, doesn't mean elementary education isn't important. It simply means there're too many elementary school teachers already.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，小学教师工资低并不意味着小学教育不重要。这仅仅意味着已经有太多小学教师了。

paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, there're few who're willing and able to perform jobs requiring a petroleum engineering major, so the value of one more of those people is very high.
paragraphs.translation: 与此同时，很少有人愿意并能够从事需要石油工程专业的工作，因此再增加一个这样的人价值非常高。

paragraphs.text: So we can have taxpayers pick up students' tuition in exchange for dictating what those students will study. Or we can allow students both to choose their majors and pay for their education themselves. But in the end, one of two things is true:
paragraphs.translation: 所以，我们可以让纳税人支付学生的学费，以换取决定这些学生学什么。或者我们可以允许学生既选择专业又自己支付教育费用。但最终，两种情况中有一种是真实的：

paragraphs.text: Either a college major is worth its cost or it isn't. If yes, taxpayer financing isn't needed If not taxpayer financing isn't desirable. Either way, taxpayers have no business paying for students' college education.
paragraphs.translation: 要么一个大学专业值得其成本，要么不值得。如果是前者，纳税人资助不需要；如果是后者，纳税人资助不可取。无论如何，纳税人都没有理由支付学生的大学教育。

questionGroups.sourceText: 中国目前拥有世界上最大最快的高速铁路网。高铁列车的运行速度还将继续提升，更多的城市将修建高铁站。高铁大大缩短了人们出行的时间。相对飞机而言，高铁列车的突出优势在于准时，因为基本不受天气或交通管制的影响。高铁极大地改变了中国人的生活方式。如今，它已经成了很多人商务旅行的首选交通工具。越来越多的人也在假日乘高铁外出旅游。还有不少年轻人选择在一个城市工作而在邻近城市居住，每天乘高铁上下班。

answer.modelTranslation: China currently has the largest and fastest high-speed rail network in the world. The operating speed of high-speed trains will continue to increase, and more cities will build high-speed train stations. High-speed rail has greatly reduced the time people spend traveling. Compared to airplanes, the prominent advantage of high-speed trains is their punctuality, as they are barely affected by weather or traffic control. High-speed rail has greatly changed the lifestyle of Chinese people. Nowadays, it has become the preferred mode of transportation for many people on business trips. More and more people are also traveling by high-speed train during holidays. Additionally, a number of young people choose to work in one city and live in a neighboring city, commuting daily by high-speed train.
